\item {[}2pts each{]}\label{enu:quad-graph} Use the graph of the quadratic
function, to answer the following:

\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}
\item What is the vertex?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$(2,5)$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the axis of symmetry?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$x=2$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the range?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$(-\infty,5]$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the domain?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$(-\infty,\infty)$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item Using the graph, what interval(s) is the function positive? (approximate)

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\approx(-.24,4.24)$\columnbreak
\end{enumerate}
\item []\renewcommand{\xmax}{10}

\item Using the function $f(x)=x^{2}-4x+4$, complete the following:

\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}
\item {[}2pts{]} Determine $f$'s axis of symmetry. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$f(x)=\left(x-2\right)^{2}$ so the vertex is $(2,0)$ and thus
the axis of symmetry is, $x=2$. (Alternatively, use $x=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac{-4}{2}=2$).\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}2pts{]} If any exist, find the $x$-int(s).

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$x=2$, where the vertex touches the axis.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}2pts{]} Find the $y$-int.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$f(0)=4$, so $y=4$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}4pts{]} Sketch the graph\columnbreak
\item []\renewcommand{\xmax}{10}

\renewcommand{\ystep}{0} %must be ymin+n

	\addplot[color=black,solid,mark=*] coordinates {(2,0)};
	
\end{axis}

\end{multicols}
\item Consider $P(x)=x^{2}-5x+2$ and $(x-2)$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item {[}4pts{]} Use division (synthetic or traditional) to find the quotient
and remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x-2$. 
\[
\begin{array}{c|crr}
2 & 1 & -5 & 2\\
 &  & 2 & -6\\
\hline  & 1 & -3 & -4
\end{array}
\]
Quotient, $Q(x)=x-3$ and the remainder, $r=-4$.\vfill
\item {[}4pts{]} Find $\frac{P(x)}{x-2}$
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{P(x)}{x-2} & = & Q(x)+\frac{r}{x-2}\\
 & = & x-3+\frac{-4}{x-2}
\end{eqnarray*}
\vfill
\item {[}2pts{]} Is $x=2$ a root/zero of $P(x)$?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []No. Since the remainder is $-4$, $P(2)=-4$. $2$ is a root/zero
only if $P(2)=0$.\newpage
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\item Use $f(x)=x^{3}-4x$ to complete the following.

\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}
\item {[}3pts{]} Find the $x$-int(s)

\begin{enumerate}
\item []
\begin{eqnarray*}
x^{3}-4x & = & 0\\
x(x^{2}-4) & = & 0\\
x(x-2)(x+2) & = & 0
\end{eqnarray*}
So $x=0,2,-2$.
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}3pts{]} Determine if the graph crosses or touches without crossing
the $x$-axis at each $x$-int.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []The multiplicity of each zero is odd; so it crosses at each zero.
\end{enumerate}

\item {[}5pts each{]} Find all real solutions.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\sqrt{x+3}=x+1$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []
\begin{eqnarray*}
(\sqrt{x+3}) & = & (x+1)^{2}\\
x+3 & = & x^{2}+2x+1\\
0 & = & x^{2}+x-2\\
0 & = & (x+2)(x-1)
\end{eqnarray*}
So $x=-2,1$. (check that these are solutions)\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item $x^{-\nicefrac{2}{5}}=4$
\begin{eqnarray*}
(x^{-\nicefrac{2}{5}})^{-\nicefrac{5}{2}} & = & (4)^{-\nicefrac{5}{2}}\\
x & = & ((4)^{\nicefrac{1}{2}})^{-5}\\
x & = & \frac{1}{2^{5}}=\frac{1}{32}
\end{eqnarray*}
\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}5pts each{]} Find the vertex of the graph of the following functions:

\begin{enumerate}
\item $f(x)=x^{2}-4x+10$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$a=1$ and $b=-4$. Use vertex $=\left(\frac{-b}{2a},f(\frac{-b}{2a})\right)=\left(2,f(2)\right)=\left(2,6\right)$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item $f(x)=-3\left(x+2\right)^{2}-5$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []Use vertex$=\left(h,k\right)=\left(-2,-5\right)$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\renewcommand{\dspace}{\vspace*{1.25cm}}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Use $f(x)=\frac{2x+6}{x-2}$

\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}
\item {[}4pts{]} Find the domain of $f(x)$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$x\neq2$, so domain: $\left(-\infty,2\right)\cup\left(2,\infty\right)$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}4pts{]} Find all vertical asymptotes.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []${\displaystyle x=2}$
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}6pts{]} Find the horizontal asymptote.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []${\displaystyle \lim_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{2x+6}{x-2}\cdot\frac{\nicefrac{1}{x}}{\nicefrac{1}{x}}=\frac{2+\nicefrac{6}{x}}{1-\nicefrac{2}{x}}=2}$
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}6pts{]} Sketch a graph of the function\columnbreak
\item []\renewcommand{\xmax}{10}
\renewcommand{\xmin}{-10}

\item {[}2pts each{]} Find the following:

\begin{enumerate}
\item $x^{2}-20$ as $x\rightarrow-\infty$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\infty$ since $x^{2}$ is even and $1>0$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item $-2x^{13}+x^{4}-50$ as $x\rightarrow\infty$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$-\infty$ since $x^{13}$ is odd and $-2<0$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item ${\displaystyle \lim_{x\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{x^{3}}}$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$0$\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item ${\displaystyle \lim_{x\rightarrow0^{+}}\frac{3}{x}}$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\infty$ ($0^{+}\Rightarrow$it approaches $0$ from the right;
so it stays positive)\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item ${\displaystyle \lim_{x\rightarrow2^{-}}\frac{3}{x-2}}$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$-\infty$ ($2^{-}\Rightarrow$it approaches $2$ from the left;
so it stays negative)\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\item The domain of $\frac{x^{2}-3x-7}{x(x-2)(x+1)}$

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$x\neq0,2,-1$. So domain:$\left(-\infty,-1\right)\cup(-1,0)\cup(0,2)\cup(2,\infty)$.\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
